subject: Residency operator scope, subprocessor roster, and export-control clarifications
messages:
From: Marta Diaz <marta.dpo@helixhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@cobaltconsulting.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Residency and subprocessor mapping for EU anchor

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Helix is moving toward an EU-anchor requirement for all PHI-adjacent inference workloads. A couple of points we need clarified before legal signs the DPA annex:

- Can Redwood commit contractually to EU data residency (processing and storage) for inference requests and logs for the Helix prod environment? If there are temporary cross-region hops (e.g., for cache rebuilds or control-plane analytics), what triggers them and how are they scoped/timeboxed?
- Please include a current subprocessor roster for the EU region and the timeline/process if you need to add a CSP or edge provider. We need to understand notification windows and the ability to object.
- Export control / international transfer: if a model patch or runtime update requires a short-lived sync to the US for build tooling, what legal/technical safeguards do you apply (e.g., encryption in transit, minimization, retention limits)?

We attached our draft annex comments; Samir from our counsel is in copy and will help redline legal language.

Best,
Marta Diaz
Data Protection Officer — Helix Health
Attachments: helix_dpa_comments_v1.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marta Diaz <marta.dpo@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency and subprocessor mapping for EU anchor

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear asks and for looping Samir in. Short answers up front, then details and attachments below.

1) EU-anchor commitment: Redwood can commit (contractually) to geographically anchoring inference request processing and persistent telemetry/log storage to EU-hosted infrastructure for Helix production endpoints. The commitment we propose is in the DPA annex and covers: customer request routing, primary KV/cache placement, and persistent logs/telemetry retention.

2) Temporary cross-region hops: we operate a scoped contingency policy (document attached) for short-lived cross-region processing. Typical triggers: automated capacity failover, emergency patch orchestration, or operator-initiated debug sessions. Conditions we apply:
- Maximum transient window: 72 hours unless mutually agreed in writing.
- Purpose-limited: only for recovery, patch delivery, or debug traces required to restore service.
- Minimization: only required token prefixes and telemetry are transferred; model parameters and full raw payloads are excluded when possible.
- Controls: TLS + customer-managed KMS for any exported telemetry; full audit trail and notification to your DPO mailbox within 24 hours of the event.

3) Subprocessor roster & change process: attached is our current EU subprocessor roster (subprocessor_roster_v2.csv). Process: 30-day advance notice for new subprocessors (standard), with a 14-day operational objection window (during which we’ll provide mitigation or escrow options), and immediate escalation paths for emergency activations. If Helix requires a hard block on a specific subprocessor, that would be addressed in the contract annex.

4) Export-control / build-syncs: For tooling or patch builds that momentarily interact with US-hosted build runners, our mitigations include:
- Encrypted transport (TLS 1.3) and customer-managed encryption for any artifacts in motion.
- Minimization: logs and debug artifacts are truncated; non-essential PII removed before transfer.
- Retention policy: transient sync artifacts are purged within 7 days by default; can be reduced in the annex.
- Access control: only named operator accounts (audited) may initiate the sync; we provide audit evidence on request.

Attachments: DPA_Annex_Residency.pdf (proposed language), subprocessor_roster_v2.csv, residency_contingency_playbook.pdf.

I'll defer to Karthik on the ops/telemetry specifics and Neha on legal notification phrasing. If this looks acceptable, we can produce a tracked-redline of your draft annex.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Marissa — quick follow-up from legal review: two clarifications before we mark the annex as 'close to final':

- Can Redwood add a clause to define what constitutes an "emergency activation" that allows subprocessors outside the EU to be used without 30-day notice? We need objective criteria (e.g., impacting >2 AZs for >1 hour, or CVE with immediate exploitability).
- For the 72-hour transient window you mentioned, will Helix get automated telemetry (a clip of the audit log) showing what was moved and why, not just a summary email? That level of detail will help our internal audit.

Thanks — if you want us to propose draft language I can do so by COB tomorrow.

—Samir
Senior Counsel, Cobalt Consulting (external counsel for Helix)

On Tue, Aug 18, 2026 at 4:10 PM Samir Rao <samir@cobaltconsulting.com> wrote:
> Marissa — quick follow-up from legal review: two clarifications before we mark the annex as 'close to final':
>
> - Can Redwood add a clause to define what constitutes an "emergency activation" that allows subprocessors outside the EU to be used without 30-day notice? We need objective criteria (e.g., impacting >2 AZs for >1 hour, or CVE with immediate exploitability).
> - For the 72-hour transient window you mentioned, will Helix get automated telemetry (a clip of the audit log) showing what was moved and why, not just a summary email? That level of detail will help our internal audit.

Hi Samir / Marta — quick ops response to both points:

Emergency activation definition (proposed operational thresholds):
- Failover due to regional capacity loss: defined as sustained (>30 minutes) loss of >25% of provisioned capacity across two or more availability zones for the region serving the customer.
- Security incident: confirmed exploit or active compromise where remaining in-region processing would delay containment as judged by Redwood SOC and customer incident lead.
- Regulatory directive: binding government order directing temporary transfer.

For any emergency activation we will:
- Trigger an automated incident record (RFC) with timestamps, affected resources, and operator identity.
- Provide a downloadable audit clip (redacted where necessary for other customers) that includes request IDs, timestamps, and the minimal telemetry for the transferred requests. This audit clip will be available in the Drive link (attached) and pushed to your DPO mailbox within 4 hours of activation.

Regarding the 72-hour window: by default we leave a conservative 72-hour max; if Helix requires a shorter cap (24h or immediate purge on completion) we can add that to the annex as an SLA term — technically feasible with a retention policy tweak and automated purge hooks.

If helpful, I can prepare a short addendum with objective wording for "emergency activation" plus an example incident report template.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
